Edit: The developers responded to this post about how to back up data, which I appreciate — that said I would like to be able to back up my data locally to be restored later locally on my computer or elsewhere as I prefer to keep my data off the cloud. title: 11+ years with this app!
body:
I’ve been using this app for over eleven years now. Let that sink in. This app is so solid and reliable and user friendly that I have been using it consistently for that long. The absolute best and most important thing about it is that it is RELIABLE. Here’s the thing about reminder apps, or calendars, or whatever: they are only worth it if you can FULLY TRUST that once you put it in the app, it WILL remind you of it when you need it to. This app does that FLAWLESSLY, which is why it’s basically a necessity in my life lol. It’s like telling a close trusted friend “hey, can you call me on Tuesday to remind me I have to do that thing?” And knowing that you don’t have to spend the mental energy worrying about whether you’ll forget it because you know they’ll do it. That’s how this works. I put it in there, and I know, without a doubt, it will let me know what I needed to remember. In ELEVEN YEARS, it has NEVER ONCE failed me on this. Let that sink in too! Eleven years of reliability. Through grad school, early career, COVID times, pregnancy, parenting, law school, more new jobs, and even more. It’s universally helpful.

Part of this I think is because of the developer’s consistent and attentive updates. I’ve used this app through many generations of iPhone, and it’s always run smooth as butter. When there are bugs (which tbh I never even noticed), I see updates come swiftly. Also, the developer has consistently developed new features that integrate smoothly into the main function of the app and make the app easier to use. Some apps when they add new “features,” it kind of thins out the main feature of the app and becomes distracting. The new features have always just enhanced the core function of the app: to know, without a doubt, that if you put something in the app, it WILL remind you when you need it to (and will keep bugging you till you do the task if you want it to… this has been essential to me 😅)

Technically I have the main features of the app unlocked free because I initially purchased it before the subscription model started, but I still choose to pay for a subscription because it’s just that essential in my life.

In conclusion, this app is absolutely worth every penny and you should definitely download it if you are looking for a good reminder app. Thank you, developer!

title: Unusable with Apple Watch
body:
Love the app on the iPhone but incredibly annoying to use with Apple Watch. If you have stacked reminders (say 5 reminders at 9 AM), the expected behavior is for Apple Watch to buzz you once and say “5 notifications on Due.” It doesn’t. It buzzes you, 5 separate times. Even more annoying is that the app waits about 5-10 seconds between each buzz, so 5 notifications mean you get buzzed every 5-10 seconds for nearly a minute at every reminder or snooze period. I’ve contacted Due support who suggested some setting changes to minimize this behavior, but ultimately said, “it’s Apple’s system, we can’t do anything about it.” 

I had 14-25 notifications throughout the day. This means none stop buzzing all day. You can’t stop it either. You can’t push a button to stop. Even taking the watch off your wrist, it will continue through the notification cycle and you just have to wait if you don’t want to be buzzed constantly. 

Some days, it uses stacked notifications while other days, for no apparent reason, the app will bother you to death. 

If you’re an Apple Watch user, try a different app.

title: If I could give it 10 stars, I would
body:
I’ve had DUE for longer than I can remember, and I’ve always loved it. It’s simple, it’s easy, and—unlike so many other apps—it doesn’t cost a small fortune. It’s an affordable annual purchase (not an endless subscription), and it does exactly what it promises, in the cleanest and most straightforward way possible.
I never write app reviews because the best apps tend to fade into the background—you use them, rely on them, and stop thinking about them. But this app deserves recognition.
Earlier this year, I was diagnosed with ADHD, and everything suddenly clicked. I realized that DUE has always worked so well for me because of how frictionless it is. When something pops into my head that I need to remember, I can instantly throw it into DUE. No complexity. No setup. No mental overhead.
What truly sets this app apart is the reminder system. I don’t use calendars, task lists, or to‑do apps anymore because things get buried, endlessly snoozed, or turned into meaningless deadlines. DUE is different. If you don’t check something off, it just keeps reminding you—gently but persistently—without you having to manage or reset anything. That “nagging” feature works quietly in the background, doing exactly what it’s supposed to do. It’s simple, effective, and honestly kind of genius.
Now, DUE is where everything goes—anything I need to remember, no matter how big or small. And the funny thing is, I appreciate this app more now than I ever did when I downloaded it over five years ago. It continues to improve, continues to get better, and I genuinely don’t know what I would do without it.
Huge appreciation to the people behind this app for keeping it affordable, simple, and incredibly effective. This is the first app review I’ve ever submitted—and it’s long overdue.

And even though the notification is the usual one line, the long press on the notification shows 8 lines so you can see that chunk of your to do list ... And you CAN select per entry the swipe-away repeat time on the reminder, so I treat that as a fourth snooze option

I also cluster my to do items by practicality categories : work, medical, house-outdoors, housecleaning, remind-spouse, long term, for-mom etc 

... And pester myself all day long for "is now a good time to deal with any of the top items on this list"

Wishlist : I wish the alarms had GPS logic and Bluetooth-beacon-logic, hey-you-got-in-the-car, let's remind you about the when-I'm-going-out list ... title: Perfect balance between a reminder app and an alarm clock
body:
I’ve found Due to be the perfect balance between a reminder app and an alarm clock. By keeping only time-sensitive reminders, it ensures you’re not overloaded with notifications or becoming desensitized to them—something that can happen with other reminder apps. Due keeps you accountable without being overwhelming.

Beyond the app itself, the customer service is exceptional. I reached out three times with specific questions, and each time, I received thoughtful responses—either the same day or the next—along with personalized recommendations on how to make the most of the app. That level of support is rare and truly appreciated.

The only thing to be mindful of when importing reminders from Apple’s Reminders app is that Due automatically marks them as completed in the original app. However, there’s a simple workaround: instead of importing everything at once, you can hand-pick specific reminders to be imported without Due marking them as complete in iOS Reminders. To do this, turn on a setting named ‘Show in Side Menu’ under Due > Settings, in a section called System Reminders near the bottom. This lets you manually select reminders before they are added to Due.

I did a lot of research before choosing Due, and I’m happy to say it works well for me. But even if it hadn’t, I can see how it would still be a great fit for many people. It has plenty of features and customization options, making it versatile enough to suit different needs and workflows. If you’re looking for a powerful yet simple reminder system, Due is definitely worth considering. 

Overall, Due is a fantastic tool for anyone who wants an effective, no-fuss reminder system that actually helps you stay on top of tasks without bombarding you with notifications. Highly recommend!

I get so busy as a college student and husband and a father of a two-year-old girl that I can get so distracted by one thing that I completely forget another thing that is also important. This app keeps reminding me until I actually get the task accomplished, so that is the primary way that it is better than simple alarms that my iPhone comes with. I can have it remind me every minute every five minutes every half hour every hour or once a week or once every two months; there are so many options. Buy it. You definitely will not regret it.

title: It’s Good But Not Worth $8
body: Overall, the app is pretty good. It could definitely use an update to the UI to make it more modern looking. Not saying that it looks bad but compared with other applications in its price range, it’s quite lacking in UI. There are also some features that I think should be better. I think that setting up the alert should be more seamless for example, when you create a new task, you’re presented with a menu to name the task and put a date for the task to be completed. If you do not do it in a particular order and click the X button in the top right of the configuration box it will automatically place the alert on your task board. In my opinion There should be a large button that says done or something along those lines. This way, the user won’t be confused about clicking the X button and accidentally placing the task on their task board and having to go back and edit it later I can provide more examples if needed. I just think the UI could use a little bit of cleanup. There should also be a category directly on the left side of the screen with the other menu items that says completed alerts or completed tasks. I find it difficult to go back and view all of my completed tasks. I like how on the iPhones reminder system you can go view the grade out task that you have completed in the past. I still use the app every day. I think it could just use some fixes and UI cleanup for the eight dollar price tag that they’re charging realistically I’d say it’s more of a five dollar app.

title: No daily Repeat Feature? Don't Force Me to Edit Review
body: From Smartshoppennycounter I am a mature customer who can read well, comprehend, and follow a three-step process. I don't understand your directions on how to use this app. I am already giving up. I purchased this subscription a few hours ago, but I'm ready to cackle in the next few hours. I only need an app that shows the simplicity of setting up reminders to repeat daily. Leave alone the weekly repeat. I have spent hours looking for the clarity of the app’s daily repeat feature, and then I am triggered by irrelevant videos in the help section. How can weekly and monthly repeat features be open and accessible to the weekly and monthly repeat gesture but not for the daily feature? How can you only set the time for the day’s reminder but have not made it available or set it up to repeat? Which one comes first? The day of the week? Are you guys kidding with people's time and money? I don't want to watch irrelevant, waste-of-time videos to figure out solutions for what I have paid for. Please implore you to fix this problem, and that will convince me to embrace your persuasive advertisements about efficiency and customer-friendliness. Thanks. Smartshoppennycounter

title: Great tool for ADHD
body: This app is amazing! It helps me keep important tasks in view so I can check several times a day to see what I may have otherwise lost sight of. With Daily Recurring Tasks, I can check each task off for today, and it will pop up for me again tomorrow. NOTE: At first I had set each task with audible alarms and snooze timing, but soon learned that drove me crazy since I use Due for so many different tasks. Now, just the time-sensitive tasks are set that way and I set mundane tasks without alarms or snooze - that way they just pop up on a list of Due items and I can quickly mark several of them done throughout the day without as many nagging reminders. I also love being able to delay the timing for tasks if I’m running behind. If you’ll take the time to understand each of the features and options I think you’ll love this app, too!

title: Must set multiple reminders for same event
body: I just found out the app doesn’t support pre-alerts at given times. For example, if I have a concert to attend June 9 at 8pm, I would want to add that appointment a single time, and then be able to have reminders 1 week before, 2 days before, 1 day before, morning of and 2 hours before. Sounds like I would need to set 5 different reminders for that. Why not just have a single even with multiple reminders? I could set up a single reminder a week before, but then I would have to snooze if for 5 days, 1 day, 18 hours, 8 hours and 2 hours, which is way too much math. Also, it doesn’t let you snooze a certain number of minutes before the event, like 10 minutes before. Instead, you have to do math again to figure out the correct snooze interval so that it reminds you 10 mins before, and that interval might not be available. This is the problem with apps that make you pay before you can try them out.

My only concern is if I subscribe and then immediately unsubscribe kinda of a paid upgrade its good for a year, but I have seen complaints involving other apps where customers are having trouble unsubscribing and continued to be billed. I'd love to see a onetime lifetime payment option offered, and would seriously consider purchasing if offered. Anyhow keep up the great work, and if for any reason the app can't be maintained, I hope Apple would consider purchasing Due and keeping it around, it's that good. The app continues to improve and impress me. I have one request, in the timers section would it be possible to add days, months, and years and custom time picker like 360 days? It would work sort of like a timer reminder.  Really appreciate this app, great job.

title: For super important tasks
body:

For me, Due is best used for my priority reminders and i use other apps for undated,  'later' or 'someday', 'projects' and other low urgency tasks.

It also works with Siri and has uncomplicated export options, which not all task apps are good at.

Highly recommend watching the less than five minute tutorial in the Help section , as I have been using the app for years, and still didn't realize some of the shortcuts the tutorial highlights.

The only two features I wish they have, is an editable notes entru field for individual reminders(like the Apple Reminders app has) and more help section screencasts. 

I thank 🙏the Due App team for creating an app I depend on to complete urgent time sensitive tasks thereby preventing me from f*ing up my life 🤪. 
P.S. the protaganist in the film 'Momento' should have definetly tried Due. 😂

title: This app would have received a 5-Star review if…
body:
UPDATE:
The developer responded to my complaint, and corrected the bug. I now have everything unlocked again! I updated my rating to 5 stars, because as I mentioned below, this is an incredible app!! Tons of thanks to the developer!!! 

They had been honest from the get go. Signing up you’re given the impression that whatever you have access to upon purchasing, you will maintain after the first year’s subscription(included in the initial purchase) is expired, EXCEPT for the new features. I’m here to tell you this is a lie. Just a moment ago, apparently one year later exactly TO THE MINUTE, I noticed my widget for this app no longer works, and I must pay the annual premium to be able to use its widgets. I now regret recommending this app to the dozens of people that I have, I feel as though I’ve misled them in some way. I see that the developer reads this stuff. This app has literally been a lifesaver, and I will continue to use it because it’s helped me manage my ADHD so well. But the lack of integrity and transparency upon the purchase is really disheartening. I’m still giving it 3 stars, as opposed to the 1 I almost gave it, because it truly is an incredible app, and has helped me have a more organized life.

title: Updated review: Found a way to stop iOS from ruining this app
body:
As someone with ADHD, Due helps me get things done. Without fail.  This app has helped me more than anything else when it comes to maintaining some semblance of normalcy.

I had previously how frustrating it was that iOS would just randomly put the app to sleep so you would go all day without realizing you weren’t being bugged.  I have found a “fix”!

Simply create an iOS automation that opens Due every day at whatever time (I set mine to 7am) and iOS is tricked.  It doesn’t actually open anything since Due is running in background, it just keeps it active.

Thank you to everyone who is responsible for this life changing app!

Surely the creators of this app would understand that not everyone needs a loud alarm?  If you’re in an environment where you can’t pester those around you with an alarm every couple of minutes.  Very disappointed in this app, spend your money elsewhere if you can or find something for free.  The app should make your phone vibrate like you’re getting a phone call, something you can actually feel.  And it should vibrate until you stop it.  Much like an Apple alarm. title: So far, so good
body:

2. Share some reminders with family members. For example, if my husband and I both have Due, I could set a reminder to “Change the bedsheets” that shows up on both of our calendars until one of us marks it as complete. If the suggestion in “1” was implemented,” then I could set a category to “shared task” and have everything in there shared between us. If this were implemented, I could insist my whole work team use Due, and set reminders that were accessible to everyone, where anyone could check it off the list. There could even be badges or kudos for people who check things off other people’s lists.

title: Does NOT allow you to add tasks by voice on watch, despite what listing says
body:
The listing for this app claims that it works with Siri and that it works with the Apple Watch. But after I paid the non-refundable $8, I learned that it doesn’t work with Siri on the Apple Watch!

It offers two options, neither of which work. The first is to use Siri to add tasks to apples native task list, which the Due app is supposed to periodically import. I tested that; it does not happen. The second option is to set up a shortcut in Siri. When I try that, the system asks permission to add the task every time I try to add one, and even when I give permission, I get an error message. 

The listing for this app should make it clear to people that it simply does not work with Siri on the Apple Watch. There is no way to verbally add tasks to this app with your watch. It is really unfortunate that I have no way to get a refund for a product that doesn’t work.

title: A must for persons with Add/adhd
body:
I have been struggling to find a reminder app that actually works to remind me since I have add. I am beyond excited to finally have found this Due app. 

All the other reminder apps seem to have maybe 1 feature of due, but none have all the key features in one like due does. 

Being able to force reminders to REMIND ME over and over is so critical for add. When I am hyper focused I may not even notice a reminder go off, and without the immediate repeating reminders I will never disengage enough to get anything done with the reminder. 

Now I can get alerts 4+ times realize I’m not going to do it right now, and then immediately reschedule the reminder for 1 hour or a day or whatever I want with 1 tap. 

And if you guys are using due, definitely use the widget! The bigger widget has short links to add a reminder and get to timers which is so convenient!!

title: Best Timer on iOS
body: tl;wr: Buy the app, get the in app purchase-- it really is that awesome. I know what you're probably thinking: "Why do I need a timer app when there's already a app included on my phone that does this?" Two words: Auto Snooze. This feature allows you to be notified when a task, reminder, or timer is due and gently nudge every so often until the task is marked complete or the time is reset. Let's say you're like me a need a reminder to stop playing video games and get back to work. I set a timer for 30minutes and an Auto Snooze of 1 minute. When my timer is up at 30 minutes, I get notified. When I don't clear the alert, I get notified at 31 min, 32 min, 33 min, and so on. This allows me to finish a level or get to a stopping point while not leaving the door open for me to play another three hours. Due is also a place for reminders and tasks that need to be completed. The "date and time picking" interface is great and easy to use. While I personally don't use this feature as much, when I have used it, it has been quick and painless. Seriously, if you ever need to set a timer or remind yourself of something AND you need a little bit of nagging to get it done, this app is the one you want. I cannot recommend it highly enough.

title: Due is the best specialty task and memory tool for me
body: Like most people, I use Due for one-off or super important tasks where I am likely to need to snooze an item (but can't forget to do it) or simply need to be reminded to do a task relentlessly. I also use Due as a manual spaced repetition system (SRS) for learning memorization where I want to be reminded of a thing I'm trying to get into my long term memory or habits. The step of putting an item into Due and then setting an initial reminder interval puts my brain on notice that this thing I'm adding to Due is important to me (just like those super important tasks I use it for). That part of my process is proactive. The other useful part comes when Due reminds me to complete a habit or recall something I'm trying to remember. "Try training the dog for 5 minutes right now!" With the ability to snooze the item I'm more likely to add something knowing I still have flexibility to delay the start time if I get slammed. And for memory items like a keyboard shortcut or learning a new piece of code it works similarly well. It's nice that I don't have to go into a separate app to "study" items. Each item I set up is quick to complete so it's not something I dread. I space out my learning reminders and habit tasks throughout my day and evening so they don't overwhelm me at a similar time and I also try to keep the total number down to 3-7 total things like this coming up per day. Each one generally doesn't take long or can take fractions of a second if you're simply being reminded of something you've already learned. Then when things get stale or ingrained as a habit I move them to a bi-weekly or monthly reminder and that keeps them in memory.

title: I love DUE, and appreciate the Apple Watch support
body:
I use due more than any other app on my phone, and it's just a great app period. 

The idea behind DUE is making sure things that MUST be done ARE done and absolutely not forgotten, while making that process as convenient and painless as possible. The goal is absolutely achieved. 

Given how frequently I use the app, I really appreciate the support of Apple Watch. Very convenient. 

It has a bit of a learning curve, but once u get it, you'll be so glad u did. 

TIP:  keep DUE permanently in your Apple Watch dock. You'll find the response time for dealing with notifications is instant. 

That's because apps in the watch dock are always preloaded and pop up ready with their data instantly

Note that you can set defaults so that you have zero auto snooze reminders (no extra bugging you), or default to any snooze reminder time you want. Further, you can set the snooze for any specific reminder, exactly as u want, regardless of how you've set the default.   This all works great for recurring reminders and individual reminders. 

You can even set up DUE to take your  reminders out of apples reminder app automatically. This let's you use SIRI to setup Apple reminders, and have them auto moved to DUE with DUE's default snooze

Also due has the great ability to let you use Siri to set up reminders that go right into due through a Siri shortcut. The shortcut will use what you say as the body of the reminder and will let you specify the time of the reminder as well, all part of the same sentence. 

Love the app

title: Unique reminder (to do) app
body:
I’m not sure this is still true, but when Due was first released, it was the only task manager on iOS that supported auto-snoozing/repeating a reminder. 

But Due has more tricks up its sleeve than just that. There’s a nifty feature that lets you specify 12 different “standard” times or periods when snoozing or scheduling a task. E.g., I have mine set of with 3 static times (8:30AM, when I’m getting ready to leave for work, 1:30PM, my after-lunch time to address urgent personal to-dos, and 8:00PM, when I’m home from work and I’ve eaten. So when I create a new to do, it’s efficient and easy to decide whether I want to accomplish this particular task as I’m getting ready to leave for work, while I’m at work (e.g., for contacting customer support for something when I know they’ll only be there during regular business hours), or after I get home. Of course you can always enter a custom date/time, but theee predefined values are a timesaver. 

I then have defined 6 dynamic periods, or lengths, of time to specify: +10 minutes, +15 minutes, +1 hour, +3 hours, +1 day, and –10 minutes, –1 hour, –3 hours, –1 day. These are displayed in the interface as buttons, so you can tap any one of them to add(/subtract) that amount of time to the cumulative length. So if I want to snooze some task for 30 minutes, I tap +15 twice. You can have any combination of static (exact) times and lengths of time. 

This is SUCH A CLEVER WAY to approach this interaction problem. As an IxD myself, I’m especially impressed. 

Due also has a very flexible yet powerful repeating task editor. There’s a log for completed to dos. You can save any number of countdown alarms each with each with a unique sound. You have the option of syncing your iOS native reminder tasks with Due (on a list-by-list basis). There are even some nice interface touches like different themes and fonts (not gimmicky, but really understated and elegant). 

Get Due! You won’t be sorry!!

title: Reminders aren't repeating
body:
I paid for this app because I have ADHD and narcolepsy and I needed an app that would remind me in advance of certain tasks and then continue to remind me until I had actually completed it, because I have a tendency to notice an alert, then promptly forget that I had something to do when it turns off. I also need an alarm that continues to go off because it's very difficult for me to wake up in the morning. Instead of my alerts repeating indefinitely, or even more than a small handful of times (I just tested it and the 1 minute snooze repeated only 9 times before stopping, I lost the data on the 5 and 10 minute snooze settings, but I've set all of my alarms to 5 min snooze before this). What ends up happening is, for example, the alarm starts going off in the morning for me to wake up, but I don't hear it/consciously register it and then after just a few repeats, it's off completely. So I don't wake up on time, and then when I eventually do, the first thing I see is that the alert went off HOURS ago and stopped. EXTREMELY frustrating.

I opened the app today (with not even any pending task notification numbers displayed on the Due badge) at random, only because I'd thought to check it, and had a LONG list of alerts that were all permanently snoozed from as far back as 2 WEEKS AGO, and I was never able to mark them as "done." Because they just turned off on their own.

I need alerts to literally repeat until I am ready to turn them off manually. To compensate for this issue I've ended up making ~six different alerts for the same task that I can't afford to forget about at slightly different times. The calendar alert system on iOS only gives me limited options to forewarn me of an event, and once it alerts me once, it doesn't alert me again, and I have to remember to reset the alert as the event gets closer. I really need an app that can do this. This app would be great if the repeat function actually repeated more than a small, set number of times.

title: Invaluable app, but rarely updated to justify subscription model
body:
LONG TIME USER HERE:

This app is the linchpin to my marriage, my job, my life. I would forget to perform vital functions without it. From the annual “call grandma” to the “don’t forget the kids at school”, this thing is a life saver. I hardly remember to pee or drink water without Due. 

My life is not too complicated so I don’t need the fancy todo apps (Things, 2Do, Omni, etc.). Due allows me to just brain dump in seconds and annoy the hell out of me until the task is complete. I love it so much. 

The user interface is beautiful the customization is great. It syncs and reminds me more reliably than any other app out there. 

However, I have been using this app since V1 and the updates are minimal. IOS has advanced and due has not evolved with it. Due does not even provide basic iOS capabilities that are now considered antiquity. The biggest complaints are the lack of a Notification Center widget, and no ability to add to due via “extensions”. These aren’t difficult to implement. The developer just does not really seem interested in regularly updating the app . 

This is is what bums me out about the subscription  model. I have a handful of apps I pay for subscriptions for, but those apps are updated at least once a month and continuously evolve with major iOS updates, offering new iOS specific features (e.g. dark mode, keyboard shortcuts, Notification Center widgets). Those updates keep me paying. 

For Due, i can count on one hand the times an update brought true change or user utility. I would gladly pay the $7 for the app. Hell I would probably pay a lot more considering my marriage/kids/job depend on it. But to go to subscription is not justifiable considering the negligible updates that have been provided over half a decade I have been using it.

title: If I could categorize reminders, this app would be perfect!
body: I use the Apple Reminders app for pretty much everything, from refilling medication every few months to setting my security system alarm every night, feeding the dogs breakfast and dinner every day to taking the trash to the curb every week. I also use reminders as a checklist of daily todos in games like Animal Crossing and Diablo 3. I wanted a separate app for gaming stuff so that I don’t have gaming badge icons on my stock Reminders app that I would end up ignoring. Due looked good because I could set individual reminders for each task and have them repeat daily. I also like that I can set a snooze timer, where if I don’t check off the task, it will send a notification again in a timeframe I set beforehand, such as 15 or 30 minutes. It’s easy to set reminders using the customizable interface where you can enter commonly-used times so you can set them with just one tap. The scrolling date and time picker is even customizable, so you can scroll through every individual minute or at five-minute intervals, etc. All of that works well. The first criticism I have is that you can only view your reminders in a today and upcoming view, where they’re listed by when they’re due. There is a sidebar with current reminders and archived/completed reminders, but there is no way to arrange reminders in lists or categories. I was hoping to arrange them nicely by game or task. I have weekly reminders to check all of the game stores for the consoles I own (PS4, PS3, Vita, 3DS, Switch), and I wanted to put all of those reminders in a single list, but they have to be placed in the same directory as my reminders for everything else. If there were an option to categorize reminders or sort them by tags, this would be a perfect app. I still highly recommend it over the other reminder apps I’ve tried from Microsoft, Google, and the other subscription services on the App Store. 4/5 stars

title: Recurring alarm notifications are clutch
body:
I set a lot of reminders like, “give cat medicine” or “wake child from nap” that don’t have to happen at a precise moment, but do need to happen within a timeframe. I love Due’s recurring reminder feature, so it can poke me every 5/10/15 minutes until I complete the task. 

This is better than setting a timer, which goes off until you turn it off, and then stops. You have to do the task right then, or else you’ll hear the timer noise until you do. Or you can turn the timer off and risk forgetting to do the task. 

This is also better than a reminder, which only sounds once, so you risk forgetting to do the task.

title: Even better than you think it will be
body:
This has really improved my productivity significantly. 

I’d be willing to bet that when the developer was thinking of names for the app, “Nag,” was considered.

Although that word has a negative connotation, this is the strength of Due. 

On a daily basis, multiple times a day, I can be heard to say, “Hey Siri, remind me to call Johnny Appleseed in three hours,” or “Hey Siri, remind me to take my antibiotic at 3pm.”

At the assigned time, I’ll get a quick notification. If I know I can put it off I just ignore it and it will keep reminding me until I hard press the notification and select done. 

Or I can snooze it for any amount of time, including hours, days or weeks. 

I do have one request for the developer: I’d like to tell the app to stop reminding me of either ALL items or at least the snoozed ones, for an hour or so if necessary. Admittedly this can be a counterproductive feature, but used wisely a user would likely be more productive when in the middle of a project, for example.

title: Best companion for someone with ADHD
body:
This app has changed my life completely! I was diagnosed with ADHD back when I was 5. I’m now 26 and in the past few years I’ve been learning a lot about my disorder. Learning things like how to remember to complete tasks on time and how to prioritize them. I’m not gonna lie, I sucked at remembering anything no matter what I did. Hence, having ADHD. Though, since I downloaded the Due app, everything’s changed. It’s like your own personal assistant hired only to remind you repeatedly of your daily tasks and to keep you on track. It’s default setting is to remind you every 5 minutes of a task you need to complete/start and it won’t stop reminding you until you act on the notification. 

Example: I set the app to remind me to upload pictures of our new employees to our website. When it reminded me I was out grabbing lunch so I tapped the “+30 min” option so it would remind me again in 30 minutes. Then when I got back from lunch it reminded me again but I was busy talking to a co-worker at the moment. So then 5 minutes later it reminded me again and I had to tell the co-worker I needed to go work on something. When I was uploading the pictures it reminded me once again but this time I tapped the “Mark Done” option. 

I know it seems like it would get really annoying but if you’re a person who’s really forgetful, this app will change your life! 

Highly recommended!!!

title: Love this app!
body:
I was skeptical at first about this app.  I was using a different app of this nature but was growing increasingly uncomfortable with it because the developers hadn’t updated it in a couple of years and the trust factor was kicking in - it had given me reasons for that.

Well, I began looking for a replacement app - online and in the App Store.  I stumbled across Due and everything I read about it and the screenshots convinced me to give it a try.  The learning curve was a little more than I expected but I quickly caught on and it wasn’t long before Due had reeled me in and I’m now hooked on this app and have deleted that other unreliable app.  

Due does what it promises - to remind you and me when it’s time to do something.  I use it primarily for reminding myself to take my meds - my schedule is complex and without Due or something like it, I wouldn’t be able to stay on track.  I also use it to remind myself about doctor appointments and physical therapy appointments plus other unrelated things.

Due is well worth the money - it didn’t take long before I was convinced and fell in love with this app!

The Due app has been phenomenal for these reasons: 1.) you can customize each appointment reminder with many more options for snooze and recurrence; 2.)  you can customize each reminder with its own unique alert sounds and the app has tons to choose from, all of which are interesting/pleasant to the ear; and 3.) the app itself is attractive—not just visually, but for its array of notification sounds and haptic feedback options. I never write these kinds of reviews, but Due is around winner (and is really getting me back on track!). — With thanks to the developer.

title: One of the few indispensable apps
body:

For example: I take medicine every day at lunch. But my lunch time varies, anytime between 11-1. I have a reminded set here for 11, and it reminds me again and again (based on an interval I select) until I mark it completed. So, at 11, it dings me. If I ignore it, or don’t hear it, or don’t have my phone on me, it will ding me again, and again, and again, until I mark it complete. This is the behavior I need. An app that reminds me once and then ends up in notifications is useless to me; I need constant reminding until I have the time and focus to mark it done.

This will be the best $5 you spend in the App Store. I’ve been using it for years now, and, as I said in my review title, it’s indispensable.

title: Another Scheduling App That’s Missing The Most Crucial Repeat Function
body:
I’ve been in business for over 26 years. For all of those 26 years I’ve had 3 monthly paper calendars on the wall of my office. Previous, current and next year. I use those calendars to mark the dates and locations of jobs I’ve booked. Every morning when I get in and afternoon before I leave, I look at that calendar to remind me of the jobs I have booked. I have not missed a job in all of those 26 years.  

Almost all of those jobs repeat on the same DAY, not DATE, each year. Imagine my excitement when I went to the repeat function. Rolled to month and saw that I could repeat reminders on the particular day (1st Monday, 2nd Monday etc) of the month I was setting the reminder for. But one more click from monthly to yearly and the availability to set reminders to repeat on a day of the month was gone.

Do you realize how many annual events repeat on the same day of the month? Almost All Of Them! From festivals to fundraisers, they do the same DAY(s)annually. Why would you create an app (a well thought out one I might add) omitting this crucial feature. I’m sure there are many businesses that book annual events. Most all annual events repeat on the same DAY OF THE YEAR. If having to go into an app every year and update the day, I may as well stay with paper wall calendars. 

After 26 years, Due came the closest to allowing me to replace my paper wall calendars with a pictures of my beautiful wife. But alas, she must still hold a less honorable location on my office wall as another app I’ve purchased doesn’t have the functionality to replace them.

Add an annual day of the year repeat function and color coding reminders and it’s a five star app for me.

UPDATE
The developer quickly responded with a work around for my above issue. Starting to load Due with my annually repeating reminders with the work around. You just earned 5 stars. Thank you for the quick response and temporary fix.

Original Review from years ago

This is a nice enough app, but definitely not worth $4.99. A free calendar apps reminder function can do what this app does.

title: Due handles all of my “performable in one action” to-do items
body:
I’ve tried many to-do apps and I now use two. One (unnamed here) for short-, mid-, and long-term goals and projects, and Due for all the rest. 

The rule of thumb I’ve devised for using Due: if it’s executable in one step, it goes into due. 

Here are some examples of recurring items and their frequency:

- Trash to curb (Sunday nights)
- Trash back in (Monday afternoons)
- Stretch + breathe (3x per day)
- Water plants (every 5 days)
- Auto debit X (5 days in advance each month, postponed each day as a daily reminder until it’s out)
- Change air filter (every 3 months)
- Change shower scrub (every 2 weeks)
- CALL: Meryl (each Sunday at 9:30am)

Here are some examples of non-recurring, one-off reminders:

- DINNER: Mark, Thai Stick
- CALL: Mom at 5:40
- DONATE: X’s GoFundMe

As a result, I no longer clutter my calendar with timely to-do items and I no longer worry that I’ll miss that quarterly a/c filter change. Really appreciate Due in my life.

title: Now an indispensable part of my life
body:
OMG. This app is actually a life saver. It is my greatest life management tool, and I have tried many. I definitely could not live without it at this point, it really has improved my efficiency and greatly reduced my stress by making it impossible to forget things. I have memory issues and this really truly helps me compensate for it and now I function much more like a normal person.

The features that made this app better than all other reminder apps:

- unexpiring repeating reminders:  I have great difficulty remembering things. They often evaporate from my consciousness once I see the notification. The fact that this app will keep alerting me over and over until I deal with it is really what saves me. No other app I found did this, so this is the most awesomely distinguishing feature for me. Also it works well because Due also has...
- super fast buttons for scheduling and rescheduling: I have to delay tasks a lot, but typing in a new date in other apps took too long. With Due I just tap-tap-tap the customizable time change options and it's scheduled in less than 5 seconds. It works well with unexpiring reminders because a task will repeat until I deal with it and yes easy to deal with it so I don't just delete tasks. 
- above feature in lock screen reveal/banner pulldown: I have an iPhone 6s and the sub menu (that I can swipe open when I get a notification on my lock screen or when I get a banner notification) lets me reschedule without opening the app. That's huge. I use it all the time. 
- natural language processing in quick add: this is killer awesome. Makes adding new tasks even faster bc I don't have to date scroll like in every other reminder app, or punch in numbers bc it recognizes dates and times in English. Those are slow and annoy me in other apps (*ahem* Todoist).
- good visuals & easy to navigate: the app is nice to look at! It makes a difference. The organization is tasks and color coding of groups of due dates ("Today", "Tomorrow", Next 7 Days", "Future") is really helpful.

I adore this app so much I want to see it get even better! Some suggestions:

- PLEASE integrate with IFTTT!!!  It would be so helpful, for example, to add my Due tasks to the Pomodoro timer app I use so I can track my progress and time spent on them. I love that app and automate a lot of my life with it. 
- there's an emoji bug where the font of text after the emoji shows up weird. As a visual person emoji help me recognize tasks more quickly and distinguish similar tasks
- integrate with Alexa (but if you integrate with IFTTT then i can do this myself 😉)

I cannot overstate how much I love this app! This is my replacement memory and makes me a muuuuuch more functional person. Thank you for fixing my life!!

title: Inspirarional!
body:
Due helps me focus on the important things when I am innundated with many things to take care of in a typical week. There is an interesting effect about writing down what to do and being reminded of it again and again as I sometimes end up not feeling like doing it. I may choose to delay it by an hour, three hours, or a day, but I actually end up doing the task eventually more than likely (I began to think more seriously about the power and benefits of writing down long-term goals and recite it every morning, too). 

Another huge takeaway from Due is its elegant design and intuitive UI and UX. I make a living as a programmer and often feel challenged or lost when trying to keep the UI clean and simple (Yes, I have enormous respect for those UI and UX designers who make this internet-driven, device-saturated 21st century a better, more livable place). I find Due a highly inspirational app especially for programmers.

title: Essential app to remain organized!
body:
I am a Microsoft Outlook junkie from the 90s through today whom constantly relies on being able to snooze an event reminder for various increments throughout the day. I don't know anyone organized enough that accomplishes EVERY SINGLE ITEM on their to-do list & within their calendar 💯% of the time....on-time...EVERY SINGLE TIME. Being able to "Snooze" a reminder for several minutes, several weeks or anytime in between (so I don't forget later) has saved me many times. Why Apple doesn't have a real snooze function is beyond me. The only suggestion I have for the developer is when Due's alarm is going off, please give us more than three snooze durations to select from. I would sincerely appreciate being able to select from six snooze durations.  Sometimes I only need 5 or 10 minutes to finish up a call; but other times I require a couple hours or may even push something back a day or two if project deadlines dictate. MS Outlook remainders have the drop down where you can select to snooze for 1,5,10,15,30, or 45 Minutes; 1,2,3,6, or 12 Hours; 1,2, or 3 Days; or 1 or 2 weeks. I sincerely appreciate being able to customize the snooze times (& all of the other customizations Due makes avail) for my demanding schedule. I couldn't properly function in the world without this essential app. 

Thank you so much, Due!!!
-C
iPhone 6+/128GB/iOS 10.3.3

title: What once was great is now worthless
body:
This was the greatest app on the app store and possibly the most valuable thing my iPhone could do untill iOS10. It would continuously remind me (on a configurable interval) until I acknowledged the task complete. I am often in a situation where I can't handle the reminder until later and can't just ask the app to snooze and may have to unlock the phone so the reminders are cleared from the lock screen. No problem before since the app would just keep on generating new reminders. 
Since iOS10 the app generated a few reminders then just stops. Sure there is a badge on the app icon but thats it. It won't even start again the next day (or whatever your next interval). It just hangs snd does nothing more until you open the app and clear the previous "hung" reminder. This is now completely useless. 
Developer, please fix this. I know it is related to the way iOS handles reminders but maybe there is some kind of re-imagening of your remind concept or a work-around that could restore this app to its once great status like on each re-remind clear the pending ones from iOS and generate a new remind. I don't think the history of the last 50 that I missed on the lock screen is that useful anyway (at least bot to me).

These alarms are 100% reliable and offer snooze functionality. Can the developers revert back to the old style notifications?
author: memark

title: Randomly Disappearing Reminders Are Bad News
body: Update - the new version has the same problem. Reminders continue to disappear randomly. This app is great, when it works. Unfortunately, it seems to simply lose reminders randomly. If I setup 25 reminders that repeat every day, it's possible that 5 of them will randomly disappear in the first month. You can't trust the app when things randomly disappear. There must be some way to protect or backup all reminders so that they can't be lost randomly? I use a lot of other iOS apps for various tasks and this is the only one that I can think of that just randomly loses important data. I would not recommend this for critical reminders until they deal with the data loss issues. Otherwise, the app is great.

One suggestion is I wish the app would allow you to organize the timers alphabetically and manually rather than just by the least amount of time to the greatest amount of time.  This improvement would align it with some of the other timer apps.   Thank you for all your efforts and continue to refine and improve.
author: Chad E Snyder

title: Was great until iOS update
body: This app was fantastic........that is until I updated to iOS 10. Previously I could set the app to continuously remind me at set intervals (1min, 10min, etc.) until I checked my due as completed. This is crucial for me since I might not be able to complete my "due" at the exact time it alarms me. I could just continue to snooze until I could complete my due. Now, it alarms me ONCE and even if I snooze, it never goes off again....rendering this app pretty much useless for me, because if I can't complete my due when I'm alarmed, I simply forget because there are no more alarms. The built in reminders app does the same thing. I purchased "Due" in the first place, because of the default "reminders" app shortcomings.  Now they are both worthless. According to the "Due" developers, this is Because iOS 10 does no longer allows the repeated alarms? WHY?? Please work with Apple to fix this......otherwise there is no point to having this app!!

title: As of iOS 10, Due no longer works

It used to reliably repeat an alarm every minute (or whatever interval you chose) until you checked off the task. It no longer does this. Ever since iOS 10, it repeats 3 or 4 times at random intervals, then gives up entirely. There is no evidence that the developer intends to fix this problem, and without this feature it's useless to me. What good is a paid reminder app that doesn't remind you?

author: Usability matters

title: It WAS helping
body:
There is a lot to like about this app, and some stuff to not like.

The incessant reminders really work for me. I never feel inclined to "cheat" by turning off a notification before the item is completed. That alone is worth the price of admission.

I love the range of notification sounds, and the interface is handsome and clean (thank you, god).

Unfortunately it takes more than intuition to figure out this app. There a lot settings that require a fair amount of trial and error. Some of the terms in the settings are confusing. For example, is a notification the same as a reminder? 

I don't like that there isn't a way to be notified ahead of an event, task, etc.

What bothers me the most is that the app doesn't sync my devices well. If I delete a to-do on my iPhone, it doesn't get synced to my iPad until I open the tablet and manually sync it. So even though I mark an item done on the phone, I still get annoying notifications on the iPad. I'm using iCloud and Box for syncing purposes.

While I want the screen to remain beautifully minimalist, it'd help to have a calendar to look at.

The bottom line is that I like this app, and it's helped me be more productive. Hopefully, the deficiencies will be worked out soon.

UPDATE (4/26/16)

I deleted this app from my tablet, and my phone is next. I could no longer take that Due didn't sync on my devices until I manually opened each of them. Also, using the notification screen functions sometimes worked and sometimes didn't. I discovered that I can put as many event notifications as I want into Calendar 5 so that will replace this. The C5 reminder concept is similar to Due's so it's easy for me to move on.

title: Not "Better Together"
body:
I am a fan of Due.

Nothing works better if you would like an elegantly designed, speedy reminder creation app (that won't quit until you've addressed them). It's really hard to miss a Due reminder.

However, I am NOT a fan of using Due on multiple iDevices, because Due reminders will not sync correctly sync between them. Not on iCloud or Dropbox sync. Ever. In my experience at least. 

What I mean is this: You can check off a DUE reminder on an iDevice. It will, fairly quickly, update to DUE on Mac/OS and acknowledge the status change. Great. I love that.

BUT then DUE on iOS will NOT acknowledge/receive an update that was completed on DUE OSX/Mac. It won't even acknowledge iDevice to iDevice? Not once in the months I've been testing it have I seen it work. 

To get sync to "work"I have to OPEN Due on EACH iDevice (if I completed a reminder on my Mac/OSX) and then check off at least one item, AGAIN.... THEN, and ONLY then, will ALL pending iOS Due reminders SYNC. If you don't do that, well of course Due will NEVER let you forget that you haven't! 

Scour DUE APP SUPPORT; you'll find quite a bit of info on how to possibly fix the issue. It boils down to several options, but primarily restarting your iPhone or iPad, turning the admittedly mercurial iCloud off/on, making sure background sync is enabled for Dropbox and correctly tweaking all the usual notification settings. Double, triple checked all parameters more times than I want to remember. None of it works.

The documentation also says an iOS bug has been submitted to Apple. It's been that way for awhile. I can't help but notice that a number of other iOS apps sync automatically with at least Dropbox and often iCloud, no problem? My guess is this particular situation with Due is more complex than I realize.

My temporary solution? Since I like DUE, I am back to using it on just my phone. Ultimately this situation is truly a "First World" problem. So simplify, right? 

It feels silly to complain about it, but I've allowed iOS and OSX to become integral to my daily workflow. So, eventually, I would appreciate a robust reminder app that "just works", without hassle, between devices.

title: Lifesaver, has issues
body:

Reminders postponed on one device almost never get updated on others , even if the app is running in background and b. Ground updated are on. I'm unwittingly knocking off two stars. 
----
Bought it in its initial 1.0 version, happily updated to the new one thanks to the dev's just update policy.
What makes this app unique among dozens of reminder apps:
*customizable in-notification snooze (1 min-1hr).(Using the notification banner without opening the app)
*set the default snooze duration for any reminder (i.e. it can nag you every minute,every 10 hrs, you get to choose the frequency for each reminder)
*Natural  language parsing, and link/phone number etc. recognition (the app asks if you want to call/or  open the link when ticking off such reminders)
Great new features:
*backgr. Sync (with i.a.p.)
*great selection of unannoying new sounds that are still perceivable.
*even easier to add reminders immediately  anywhere in the app, including from the search box, using plus button 
*easier, customizable time manipulation presets on the add screen
*URL scheme & callback support
* Even greater, minimal yet super-intuitive and optimal design.

The app does crash every now and then while modifying reminders, but I'm sure a fix is on the way (very frequent updates)
Other than that, nothing but greatness, an app worth way beyond the asking price. 

 X-callback url support
*link & phone number recognition in your reminders (makes them tappable to instantly open the page/ email the person / call the phone) 

There's a lot more to this app that makes it singular than a few pros I listed above, if you don't see the difference with other apps, think it's overpriced, etc. you're really not looking closely enough. Go check out the dev.'s webpage.

title: Hands down my most used app. Love it!
body:
This app has had a significant positive influence on my life. It has helped me keep on top of my very busy schedule by gently, yet persistently reminding me of appointments or of routines like when to pick up the kids from school. Even more, it has helped me establish healthy habits by reminding me of things I value but sometimes forget to make time for (exercise, going to bed early, etc.)

It does one thing very, very well--easily reminds me of something that has a specific due date or specific recurring time. It is easy to postpone reminders (buying the app gives you much better options for this than the free default) that don't go away unless you deliberately mark them completed. 

It doesn't take the place of an app like ToDoist or other general list making apps that are helpful for categorizing projects. I need both apps. 

Due is just so easy and elegantly designed that I use it all day long. As a bonus, it works great on the Apple Watch, gently tapping my wrist to remind me to pray, or go to bed now, or send in that sick note for my son. 

It's much more cumbersome to add entries like this to the calendar app, plus I don't want my calendar cluttered with daily routines. Rather, I save the calendar for appointments. 

Due app has truly transformed my phone to a highly efficient productivity tool. It also has wonderful potential for those with ADHD, especially students. 

I use it throughout the day and have no idea what I would do without it. It gets my highest recommendation.

body:

Anyway, long story short, buy this app. It's awesome and does exactly what is says it does. 
Creating reminders or timers is no hassle at all and only takes a few seconds at most. The design is gorgeous and perfectly matches iOS 7/8, and functionality is simple but effective. Due easily conquers the native Reminders app, and has even taken place over calendar apps for me. 
If you're on the fence about it, just buy it. I did and am so happy I did. Honestly, just think that I took the time to rewrite a 5-star review after losing one only a matter of minutes ago. Clearly I must really like this app. Yeah. 

My only suggestion to developers: incorporate a location-based notification system. These really come in handy sometimes, and I would love to consolidate to this one app instead of needing to use another for that purpose. Thanks! 😁 
(Praying that this review won't be lost unlike the last... 🙏💩)

title: Extremely well designed and smart
body:
Due's killer feature is the way the reminder snooze works. For certain tasks I want a relentless snooze to reappear at custom intervals and be functional from the lock screen. That's where Due excels. The timer feature is great too, allowing multiple concurrent timers. With Dropbox sync and a good Mac companion app, it does everything I want it to. First home screen app, for sure.

The only improvement I'd suggest is standardizing the pricing because there's a confusing in-app purchase for additional alert tones that bills itself as an upgrade from version 1. I never had v1. I purchased it anyway and it gave me access to the tones. It just left me asking, "was this a bug that I was asked to buy an upgrade right after buying the app?" I wrote Due's support and never got an answer to my question. The app continues to work great though so I'm keeping 5 stars. 

A word of caution, don't go overboard by creating too many reminders when things are not truly due by a certain time. Don't put your entire project and task system here. Due is relentless and you'll quickly find yourself outmatched and stressed under a pile of snoozed reminders. An example of what I use it for is a reminder every couple of hours to get away from my computer desk and take a short walk. I appreciate being able to snooze it and know it's going to come back and bug me to take better care of myself.

title: Awesooooome!!!
body: I've spent about $30 on organization Apps over the last two months, and this App adds the most value / has the potential to add the most value to my life.  Beautiful to use, organizes my mind dumping yet I still feel in control.  Organized "Due app" reminders by 3 colors/sections in the vertical list of entries/rows:  Past due, soon due, and due a while away from now.  Ability to reincarnate past reminders by simple swipe.  If do a 'loooong swipe' the. totally deletes.  Then have a several second chance to hit "Undo" banner that appears at bottom of screen.  Parses a sentence like "bla bla in 5 minutes" and then gives you the Option of translating the 'time part' into the time setting by hitting a gray banner that expands into some of the space of the central 'tapper' box thingie.  Allows for customize your 'tapper' box thingie to add or remove time to a due date.  Also cool that ability to include 'time points' to this 'tapper' box thingie.  Reminder/Alarm title can span multiple lines and just does its job to accommodate the entry row size as you type, and for the completed entry.  Can search past reminders - potential here.  Also can use the separate list for "timers" and can keep reusing these super easily because a 'short swipe' recycles an entry here.   A ton of different new alarm sounds that aren't all annoying, yet annoying enough to be an alarm.  One thing to add maybe is ability to vibration alarm and to customize the pulse like in iPhone settings.  Bailing out of making an alarm accomplished by tapping on the Red part of table and then somewhere in the gray space above.  A substantial screen you're taken to when scheduling repeating reminders, yet not overbearing.  The button layout is not overbearing in that the options I see are ones I would miss is they were gone.  Editing an entity is easy because the extra buttons involved (to do more than streamlined process of simply creating the alarm with the proper time setup) are arranged Also in the middle of the screen, surrounding the box.  Also the buttons are circles which make sense to tap.  Not an excess of horizontally scrolling screens, however menu can be accessed at any point and covers like 2/3 of screen horizontally.  Then can be unswiped/ un-rolled over the screen.  That menu has items like "Reminders" and "Logged" and "Timers".  Not an excess of buttons.  The additional buttons come into play when making the reminder - when I Want them to.  Now you can see your iPhone reminders in the App through the menu, so can easily turn one of Them into these "Due app" reminders.  The bright Red and Green of the sliding of an entry to delete or recycle, mix vividly with the grays and slightly dark red colors of the App.  Nothing hard on the eyes to quickly do your thing and know it worked.  This app fulfills a niche and does it well.  Keep on pushing those tasks forward!  Whew procrastination! -- which actually is often just the symptom of an under-understood way some minds work.  This app helps people who need that constant reminder - because then maybe it will come when the time is Actually right.  Not a Single chance, this app will not stop until you tell it to.  And it won't persist in an annoying way either.  It's not snooze and you loose here.  It's snooze with good judgment or something, and then actually Finish the thing your brain is invested working on, and Then continue forward (without being pestered by loud noises that drone on for minutes at a time).  Combine this app with Launch Pro and you're good to go.  I also recommend Fantastical and DayOne.

title: Still good, but trending down
body:
First, this is the best productivity app in my arsenal of 30+ similar apps.

It augments a serious weakness of mine and makes me better.  I set reminders for tasks that must not slip through the cracks: critical meetings,  paying bills each month,  remembering there's ice cream in the trunk, remembering the chore I promised my wife I'd do the next day, etc.

When a reminder triggers, I snooze it until I get it done. Sometimes I snooze for a minute and sometimes for a week.  That, along with ease of use and good recurrence settings, is the strength of this app.

There are two reasons I withheld a star. First, the app used to be better.  With the major update to refresh the UI, it now takes more UI manipulation to perform the most common operations when running the app.  Second, I have been unable to get notifications to appear since that same update.  When a reminder triggers, my phone makes a noise, but there's no pop-up and so I have to launch the app to check my reminders.  Notifications are on for the app in system settings and the app itself, but they don't work.

My only complaint is how you have to set the time for a new reminder. I like the grid style for when I need to edit a current timer but not when I first set one up. It requires too many extra steps. title: Complicates the interface compared to version 1
body:
I use Due a lot, and was glad to see a big update that improves syncing issues and looks good on different screen sized. But I generally find the interface to be s step back from version 1.

Clicking to edit a time now brings up a big, white grid or options instead of a few option within the main list. First, that's a bit disorienting since it feels like a big context switch just to, say add a delay. The grid itself is a little overwhelming. All the buttons look the same and feel a bit disconnected to the time they are editing above. The big default scrolling time picker is cumbersome, but very clear. This grid is trying to emphasize maximum flexibility for "quick changes", but makes me hesitate before I click anything. I may get used to it over time, but frankly it feels slower than the more intuitive interface from before.

There are a number if circle icons buttons that I also confuse. Is X delete or cancel or go back? What's the difference between OK and the checkmark. While I can figure all these out when I think about it, I shouldn't really have to think about it. More standard UI controls like Back and Done button, and recognizable "check marks" would be much easier to work with.

Finally, the tab bar to jump to different sections of the app was replaced with a hamburger and basement menu. This gives more vertical space, but now requires two clicks and an animation to switch anywhere. Not a good trade off for me.

title: Was a happy Due 1 user...
body:
Ok, first off, I love to buy apps and support my favorite developers, and $2.99 is not a lot of money in the grand scheme of things. 

That said (and maybe I need psychiatric help), I cannot believe how aggravated I was after I started a timer and was then hit with an in-app purchase screen when I tried to pause the timer! Seriously, $2.99 to pause the [explative deleted] timer!

So here's my problem: this upgrade request interrupts a user in the middle of a time sensitive workflow and is completely disruptive and unnecessary. Even if I wanted to pay $2.99 to support the developer that definitely was not the time to do it. If a developer wants money for a feature, it should be clear at the outset that the tool cannot be properly used without the upgrade *before* the user needs it in a time sensitive context. 

Requiring money to allow a user to pause a timer seems like such a scammy way of encouraging people to pay for an app. I understand a lot of the other features requiring payment before use, but pause? Come on!

Psychology is a funny thing. I probably would have paid upfront for the upgrade but because of the disruption caused by the in-app purchase request, I'm deleting the app, using another timer, and leaving a bad review. Weird, I know. I guess I like supporting class acts and have a problem with tactics that feel even slightly scammy.

title: Needs push notification syncing
body:
Another update:
So turns out after further testing that Due must be open (can be in background) on any devices you want the sync to be "immediate" on. Otherwise, it will eventually update via background refresh. This is disappointing and I have to drop a star since it seems that push notification updates aren't implemented after all. I'm surprised that there is no app on the App Store that takes advantage of this feature that's been available since iOS 7.

Updated comments:
Sync is definitely still a little buggy. My other device doesn't always pick up changes made from the original device. For instance most recently, I tapped "Options -> View" from a notification, then postponed it by 1 day from within the app. But my other device continued to alert me until I manually opened the app on that device.  This happens probably 25-50% of the time. Hopefully that will be fixed in a future update. 
---
2.0 is a great update and the latest release improves on it further. This is the only notification app I'm aware of that appears to take advantage of push notification sync (which allows for almost instant sync across devices, instead of the random background update that most other apps use if they do even that). Instant sync is important for a notification app when you're snoozing and adjusting alert times that are due in the near future, otherwise you end up with the same reminder going off at different times across devices which is really annoying. 

The extra auto-snooze time choices (instead of just 1 minute or 1 hour) are also a very welcome feature that no other current app provides. 

My only request is for Siri/Reminders integration  (automatic like Fantastical, not the manual import) so that I can add reminders without having to open the app.  This would be extremely useful for this app. I understand Reminders doesn't support all the advanced features that Due does, but any reminders added through Siri could still go by the configurable default settings.

title: Still a very useful app
body: Was a great app, then there was a big overhaul, some good, some bad.  Still waiting to see what the next update can improve on
author: justap77

title: New update terrible
body: The new update is so annoying! The original was so elegant, simple and intuitive. The new interface is cumbersome. Why ruin a good thing?
author: Me5678654248

title: Don't like the new interface and ads
body: I don't think the UI should expose things like the pause button, only to show me an ad to pay for the feature. Each time this happened is misleading and disappointing. Same thing about setting snooze to anything but 1 minute and 1 hour. Yes, you deserve money for your hard, and potentially excellent work (like the first UI). But this is not the way to do it. I will look for another app to do what I want without misleading me.
author: gigacoconut

title: Amazingly Effective
body:
This simple app has transformed my ability to guarantee that tasks big and small get remembered and done even when I am very busy. 

It's the little things that matter here. Very easy to use. Compared with iOS reminders, the reminder will be less intrusive, but will repeat ("auto-snooze") at an interval you can select when you set it. This is critical: a small tap on the shoulder at the desired interval until you clear it. 

With auto-snooze at 1 minute, I even like this for waking up in the morning.
author: Purdueprof

title: Love It!
body:
I used Due for a couple of tasks before the update, but once I got used to the new UI I started looking for tasks to add to this app. 
I really like the color coded timeline list of overdue and upcoming reminders, and that you need to click on a task twice to mark as completed or snooze - this was too easy before and would result in tasks being marked done on accident. 
I just wish we could use Siri to add reminders into Due (I know this is not the developers fault). 
I hope everyone will buy the in app update, because you can tell a lot of thought and work went into Due2.
author: Alphalicious

title: Believe the negative reviews.
body:
Used this app on a daily basis. This "update" cripples functions that were available before. Now I can't even pause a timer before it asks me to pay for a feature that was already there before the "update". I understand developers have to make money but this isn't the way to go about it.

For example, If I had bought an alarm clock with a snooze feature and then the manufacturer decides to "update" it and gives me another alarm clock with no snooze feature unless I pay extra, is that fair? 

In any case, I have already deleted this app and I don't see myself ever using it again.
author: Kance

title: Great reminders app
body: When something has to get done, this app helps me make sure I do it. Love the auto-snooze options and snooze or mark as done right from the notification!
author: Lizandan

title: iPad versus iPhone?
body: I got the update and paid the price. Yet my iPhone will automatically adjust to Dropbox-synced updates (and vice versa) from my Mac, but not my iPad? WTH?
author: JayWigley

title: Was great
body: This app was amazing but the update traded a sleeker look for basic functionality
author: Bat*Man

title: Best snooze design I Use Every Day For Meds, Parking,
body: I needed an app to help me remember to take Meds and tried a bunch.  This is best for me bc it rings and it so easy to snooze it for an interval.  Also it rings once every min until you deal with it, so if it goes off when you're away from phone, you'll catch it again.  Finally design for setting quick alarms for rings like parking is fantastic.   Love love love.
author: mnanda

title: New update two steps backwards
body: I've used Due for a coupel of years but am very dissapointed in the new interface, wiush I could go back to the old one.  When an item was due, it used to pop-up on the lock screen, but now it doesn't.  I  used to be able to dismiss an item by single click, now I have to click and click again in another box.  Please add the ability to dismiss again with one click (as an option).
author: Mikepa

title: One of my favorite apps.
body:
Didn't think much of this app when I first downloaded it. It seemed kind of basic to me. Turns out thats why I like it so much. If you need to remember to do something, just key it into this app and it will pester the hell out of you until you do it. Love it.
Update 01/27/15. 
When the new update came out a couple of weeks ago I did not like it but decided I would give it a try before I commented. After 2 weeks I can positively say this update is a mess. The developer took an app that was simple and easy to use and over complicated it. Sure the app could have used an updated look but he changed the basic operation of the app which was so simple. Before when I needed to remember something it was so simple to whip out my phone, type what I needed, pick a time and shove it back in my pocket. Acknowledging alarms was just as simple, but he screwed that up too. He also took away all audio feedback. Before when you cleared a "due" you got a sound now you get nothing so you really have to concentrate on what you are doing. 
Please bring old version back. In meantime I am switching to Alarmed.
author: Petypop

title: App keeps crashing
body: Interface looks a little bit better.. I prefer the old one. New app keeps on crashing
author: E163

title: Asks for money more often than my kids
body: This use to be a pretty good app. Since the upgrade it can't do even the simplest of tasks without asking for money. Now it's worthless.
author: blankman66

title: Working for me
body:
This app is irritating! It reminds me over and over until I do the items on my list. The author needs to fix that.

Just kidding. It actually does annoy me, and I'm using that to get things done.

One hint: the time entry gizmo felt incomplete until I noticed that a tap on the red summary line brings up a standard date/time picker.
author: Fjhdsgjjfc

title: Used to love it--until the update
body: I paid $5.00 for this app months ago (and I rarely pay for apps). I used it daily and loved it. It was simple to use. Now it's cumbersome, not as user-friendly, and filled with too many choices. And I have to pay more to unlock other features?!? Wow, I'm disapponted.
author: Lolynn2

title: Difficult and now risky to use
body:
The original version of this app was the single best app purchase I've ever made. In fact, if I had to delete every single app on my phone but one, it's the one I would keep. The new version, however, is far less useable and I may switch to a different reminder app. The two key problems for me are 

1. To tick a reminder done you swipe left, but to delete the reminder completely you swipe left "fast". I live in constant fear that a critical repeat reminder will get deleted accidentally. In fact this has happened but I've noticed and used the undo feature, but at some point I know I won't notice and I will lose it completely. 2. The sleep function is the key feature for me. I set a due for 10 am and then maybe I'll move it back an hour or two due to my work flow. Now, this is a multistep, tap and swipe process that takes more steps and is far less handy.
author: CK and the boys

title: Is there a way to go back to the old version?
body: Loved the old version.  This 2.0 version is a step backward.  It's the typical form over function upgrade.  More whiz-bang design meant to impress other designers rather than added functionality to help the user. The little bit of new functionality in this upgrade could have been added to the slightly spruced up old version interface and been very useful.  Now it takes me three steps to make simple time changes when it used to be a one-step process.  There used to be a distinction between a brief postponement and major a reschedule.  Now one most go through all the steps of the latter to perform the former.  I'm looking for a replacement.
author: N8VZ

title: Adds unnecessary required swipes for things the last version did automatically
body:
The app looks better and everything is better, except one thing that makes the whole experience worse than the last version. You have to swipe to confirm things you didn't before, things that happened automatically. For example, if you delay a notification. Significantly less convenient. And baffling why that would be added when it takes more effort and the last version did it automatically in a single touch.

Please change this. Would be 5 stars if not for this unnecessary problem.
author: J0HNBLAZE

title: NO Alert Sounds?
body: I am not certain the benefit of a reminder app if there are no sounds working. I even upgraded without any benefit • there are far better reminder apps free than paying for one: if I ever get an email back having reported the issue days ago I might update this review until then avoid is the best review I can give.

title: Love
body: I love you Due
author: KING EDWARD EMPIRE

title: Jazzy

author: hsoarez

title: Will be discontinuing use because of update
body: I've used this app for over a year, loved it. The update however is terrible. Takes way too many steps to check something off, design is inelegant, and every time I open the app it tells be I need cellular data, if I'm on wifi why would I want it to use data?
author: Hbehrens5

body:

Due is my personal "nag" but in a good way. I put every important event into Due and have it "nag" me until I complete the job. This app has saved me time and money.

body: With the introduction of iOS 8 I have found myself very much wanting a good reliable reminder app again. I had tried to DUE before but it did not meet my needs. This version has worked great, it has been easy to set up reminders & repeat notifications have worked flawlessly and even the synchronization between my iPad and iPhone has been fast and accurate using the Dropbox option. I'm highly recommend this reminder app if you're looking for one that will take care of in iOS 8.
