title: Ruined by UI
body: The old version was nearly perfect except for sync. This version updates sync but comes with a confusing new UI which makes the app not worth using. It adds steps and lots of complexity to what was previously a joy to use.
author: DouglasGottlieb

title: Previous version was perfect
body: The previous version of the app was excellent. However, this update created a confusing app,  that's not user friendly, and not easy to program.  For instance how do you only select 3 reminders for a day? I can't find the way to remove the fourth reminder. I had to stop using it.  Missing the old version.
author: Eddie528

title: Best app ever

title: Crippled in update
body: What was a simple, powerful, efficient timer and reminder has become a needlessly complex hash with the addition of annoying in-ap-purchase screens which interrupt functionality. Due has lost all value.
author: fdp3

title: Stole my old app, and my money.
body: Had the old version of due both on iOS and on Mac.  My old version was now replaced (instead of just starting a new app named Due 2?).  Now I've lost all my syncing abilities as well as losing the app on iOS unless I pay the decided ransom of $2.99 to get it back, otherwise I'm forced to use timers I can't even pause.  If Apple did this with my phone it would be theft; if Nike did this with my shoes, it would be theft; yet Due just did this and it's trying to tell me "Welcome to the Improved Version" and it was neither 'welcoming' nor 'improved'.
author: hufriedy

title: Finally a full function reminder app!!
body:
I don't normally do reviews. But this one certainly earned it. I have searched and searched for a high power reminder app that would let me configure individual reminders any way I needed to. Due 2 does just that. No more choosing only between 1 minute or 1 hour auto snooze. No more delaying a reminder and having it affect all the future repeats of that reminder. No more having to set 10 different fields to input a single reminder. Due 2 solves it all!!

Thank you for a job well done!!  I am excited to see what enhancements you have in store for the future.
author: Gary8744

title: Not as simple as before
body: I've used Due for a long time and it has been my constant companion for getting things done. I work in a very time sensitive business and the extra steps (at least it feels like extra steps) to do things like snoozing an alert are annoying. Of course I'll keep using it because nothing comes close to the core functionality but not a 5 star anymore.
author: Ainkor

title: Previous version was better
body:
I was excited for the new version, and willing to pay the in app purchase to support the developer of my favorite reminder app. However, the quick postpone button "10 minutes" "1 hour" later, etc. is no longer quick. One is brought into a menu where the user can still do that (plus pick a specific time) but now I have to think about it because of more options, and also take another tap and pick "only for this occurrence" or "for all future". I like the old way where I just hit a button and it assumed I meant only this occurrence. If I want to change for all I'd edit it. But that simplistic awesome feature is gone. Guess what?! I am reverting back to the previous version. How disappointing.
Please fix! I'll check for future updates to fix this.

BUT I WILL NOT ‼️‼️SPEND ANYMORE MONEY ON YOUR APP‼️‼️
author: graystar77

title: Lost its simplicity
body:
Gave it a shot but there are too many things that make it more complicated to use for no gain in functionality or usefulness.

- Snoozing interface is cumbersome now. Lots of choices for something that used to have a few. Do people really use negative snoozes??? Do you really need that many options? It was so easy to snooze by increments of 10 mins.

- Have to swipe to save changes or snoozing. It used to save automatically. Also, there's no Save button as an alternative to swiping. You used to be able to snooze with two taps near each other. Now it's two taps far away from each other and then a swipe.

- Have to swipe to complete a todo. Should also be able to simply tap.

- Hamburger nav is a poor UX direction. There are only five items in there. They could be five (or fewer) tabs at the bottom. Much easier to reach on the 6 and 6+.

- Just me or is Search too easy to activate? I never use search but it's always getting activated when I scroll up the list.

title: Nice App....But
body: Just downloaded the app. Went thru all the info. Started using, looks real nice... But!!  Would love to have "Set time" for a reminder. Nice to be able to set reminders for a day, but would love to be able to set a "time" for each reminder, not just a set time for each day.  Thanks.

title: Frustrating update

The worst is recurring notifications — every time you push ‘take meds’ ahead 1 hour it asks you to confirm this for 'only this instance' or 'all future instances' and it’s very easy to select the undesired option. Too much thought was put into visuals and not enough into usage.

The best money I've ever spent on an app!

body: My wife and I both used this app. We were disappointed with the update, Extra steps  to close or postpone a task.  interface not as intuitive, at the start.  After many years of using this app, I'm looking elsewhere.
author: gregj1258

title: Got complicated!
body:
It got complicated after this latest update. I want to keep it simple and less options to choose from. That's how Due app is before.

Not sure why I still upgraded and paid for $2.99. I thought there's more.
author: JACo_OLz™

title: No longer a great app
body:
I tried hard to love this update, but unfortunately something great was lost this week. The author threw away the brilliant interface that made "Due" so quick and easy to use. 

Once upon a time, your most-used tasks were quickly and easily accessible from you main list. But now you have to switch between two different pages and it takes four clicks just to delay a task. I know that doesn't sound like a lot, but it's a major part of this app, and now it's disorienting.

That's unfortunate. I used this app more than all other apps on my phone combined (no exaggeration). But I have to move on. 

Thank you to the author for many years of great productivity. I hope you find your way back to restoring what once made "Due" a truly brilliant piece of programming. You will be sorely missed.
author: R. Charles

title: Long Time User
body: I've used this app for several years! Unfortunately I am forced to re-purchase this app @ $4.99 + $2.99 because id like to change the "notification" of "every minute", to "every 15 min". Since I had moved since I originally purchased the app & had to change my Apple ID due to having a new ISP, this app won't allow me to pay the $2.99 for the upgrade because it was purchased under a different Apple ID. So BEWARE: if you've moved or changed your Apple ID since buying Due 1.0 then U'll have to re-purchase this app (2.0), and lose all the data you had on Due 1.0.

title: WAS Great. NOW ruined. Pay AGAIN?
body:
Not too happy with new version.

That would've been a lot more useful. I would happily paid for NEW features, not PAY AGAIN for existing features. [duh]

author: NortheastGuy

title: I loved old version- hate new version
body: New app update looks nice but if you want to push back the time of the reminder takes 3 clicks. When you are in a hurry it feels like an eternity. So frustrating. I want to just do one click to push it back so I can move on with what I'm busy with. Old app was so much more simple and easy. Please bring back the simplicity of the old one!
author: Bvbash

title: Great Update Falls Short
body:
First off, I'm glad we finally have this update. I like the new icon and the new interface but there are a few glaring changes that I immediately miss.

When I got a reminder, I had the ability to tap on it and add minutes, hours, or days without having to go to a different screen. I could also double tap for other editing and options. Now, it feels more cumbersome and not as fast. I use to be able to do it quickly without having to keep my eyes on the screen. Now, I have to look at a different screen and a grid of choices.

Also, I don't like having to swipe to the left to get to my Log and Timers. It was easier and more convenient to tap on an icon at the bottom because I used those sections frequently. I could do it with one hand. I wonder if the developer took into consideration that having bigger screens make additional swiping and tapping harder for those who have shorter fingers and reach. But, I am glad the "Undo" is now at the bottom instead of the top. 

Finally, I miss the sound effects when you add more time or mark a reminder done. They were very helpful.

That said, Due is still my favorite "reminder app" especially now that additional snooze time increments have been added. I use it daily in addition to a "GTD app" because I haven't found an app yet that does both very well.
I hope the developer considers bringing back these features and then I can give it four stars.

title: Great reminder app
body: I have several things that I do on a regular basis that I would often forget without reminders. title: Ruined a good app
body:
I was really excited to read about the changes. Most were exactly what the app needed, at least how they were described. 

-- background sync so you don't have to open the app on each device when an alarm alerts.  Sadly this doesn't work. 
-- option to alert at something greater than 1 min and less than 1 hr.  This doesn't work either
-- new interface to make it easier to create, edit, and snooze.   This fails on this.

title: Will take getting used to. Not as easy to use anymore...
body:
I have had this app forever and loved it for the most part. Ease of use and how quickly you could do things with a tap or two was great. 

Now with this update all that is gone. Well its still there, but a lot harder to use. Too many choices sometimes can make the app too cluttered. And that is exactly what happened here.

I had addressed with the developer a while back about why the snooze is only either a minute or an hour and not 5,10, 30 minutes etc. At that time he had given me a long explanation about how the other developers do it wrong, how apples software is designed a certain way, how he knows what he is doing and that is what makes him different. Well now all of a sudden different snooze times show up and they are an in app purchase for $2.99!  What a way to make money!!!

Also where other apps give free snooze tones or sounds, here we have an in app purchase.

In my opinion yes the app needed a new modern look and feel but the functionality should not have been compromised.  This will be just way too complicated for people who loved the simplicity of this app.

title: Handy reminder app
body:
I've switched most of my recurring reminders to Due primary for the repeat alerts and snoozing features. The URL scheme functionality is great for geeks. The interface takes a bit of getting used to, but you eventually figure it out even if it remains less-than-intuitive. Running multiple timers is also a huge plus.

The real key I've discovered lately to using Due is to dump all your must-do tasks into the app. All of them, large an small. Because the task list reorders based on "next up", it's super easy to see what you have to do and reschedule if need be. Even if you know you need to get groceries today, add it. That way you can see where it fits into the day with other items. 

I recently requested an addition of an optional text description under each item that describes how far away the item is ("in 3 hours", etc). And editing a task is a bit convoluted, especially if you want to move it to an earlier time. 

Still, it's a superb app and the more you lean into it, the more you realize this.

title: Picks Up Where Native App Left Off
body: This app is limited only by its prerequisite—iOS—in that it only allows for auto-snoozing every minute or every hour.  There are many reminders that I would like to be reminded about every 15 minutes or so instead of every single minute, but I cannot fault the creator of this app for that shortcoming, as iOS greatly limits his ability to work within a broader range of auto-snooze times.  I have always looked for an app that would continue to notify me of a reminder until I actually physically marked the reminder as complete.  The native app simply leaves so many notifications to chance in that it assumes you are looking at your iPhone’s/iPad’s screen when the due time comes around.  Well, life doesn’t work that way, so that’s why it is great to have an app that will continue to remind you of missed notifications.  The only reason I haven’t given this app five stars is because of its steep price for what I would consider to be quite a minimal amount of flexibility.  Having reminders in separate “reminder categories” would improve my rating of the app, but four stars ain’t bad.  And, to boost, the UI is very nice with iOS 7.

body:
I am a physician with a very busy schedule and very poor organizational skills. This is the only app I've been able to find that doesn't require you to REMEMBER to look at your todo list in order to recall what you should be working on. 

Here is how I use the app:

1. I get a task

2. I think about when I'm likely to be able to do it (after office hours, during lunch, etc)

3. I put the task in due and tell it to remind me AT THE MOMENT I THINK I'LL MOST LIKELY HAVE TIME TO DO IT. 

4. And if I can't do it when the app reminds me; it's not a problem. Due will automatically remind me each hour that I still have a task to do. Or I can just quickly choose a new time and go on with my day. 

Give this app a try. There's nothing like it out there.  You may just surprise your coworkers with how good your memory suddenly becomes.

title: Love the reminders, but editing tasks is a pain
body: Love the reminders, and the persistence of the app in nagging me to complete tasks. Definitely the best out there at that, except for maybe the BugMe app which has more intuitive snoozing and hand written tasks. Due does have one area where I think it could improve, though: editing of existing tasks. I wish there were a one-click edit button for each task like there are time-advance buttons. It is a pain to have to click Edit in the top menu and then choose the task to edit. I want to be able to either long-press the task, left-swipe and then choose edit from the menu choices (just as many clicks as the current method, but more intuitive) or have a button right next to the snooze options.  Maybe you could condense the size of the buttons down to make room for an edit button?? Also, it would be nice to be able to add stars to tasks to call them out as critical. Lastly, why can't I see my lists in full screen or close to it? Currently, the list takes up the right 2/3 and the Reminders/Timers/Logbook on the left occupies a small strip, leaving a 1-inch or so grey bar just right of those buttons and left of the task list. Why not allow for more space for reminders by using that grey area?? Hope you take my suggestions into consideration. Love the app in general!

title: Awful, but beautiful UI
body:
You can be forgiven after you waste 5x the normal price for a lifestyle app and buy Due. It's truly beautiful and has some innovative controls that let you do much in a single click. Unfortunately however, it has a couple of glaring deficiencies that within 72 hours will make you regret your purchase. 

First, it can't log the completion of recurring reminders. At all. One shot reminders when completed go in a downloadable log, but when you complete a recurring reminder it zips off to the next interval as if it never happened. Trying to remember if you took your vitamins before bed? You won't be able to be sure. And how many of your most important reminders are recurring? Lots of them. 

The other odd thing is you don't have any intervals for things like reminders other than minute, hour or day. On the control where you can choose, Due's otherwise exquisite UI has an ugly stain where the developer blames apple for not providing not granular control. That's really odd and seems disingenuous. I have a couple of other apps that do interval timing and they all offer variable interval reminders and snooze values. Why is Due so different? Why blame Apple?

title: Misrepresented in Description, Does Not Sync, Reminder Frequency Not Configurable
body:
I have memory problems. I bought this program for my iMac, iPhone and iPad to remind me throughout the day of things I have to do. If I forget, even once, to complete some of these tasks, it results in serious health consequences. 

This program has two major flaws that make it essentially unusable for me and is causing me to find another app altogether to take its place.

First, the app description is inaccurate. It says it syncs through the iCloud. It is a "fake" sync that doesn't work, despite the company's many troubleshooting pages. This is a clear tipoff that even the manufacturer knows there's a serious bug. This bug has persisted for months, they have chosen not to fix in an update--or perhaps they are unable to fix it (either way, they need to stop misrepresenting this app in their description that it syncs with iCloud). I, like many others, have followed their troubleshooting pages (plural) with no success.

Applications that sync with iCloud include Apple’s Calendar, Contacts, and the third party app Things. On these applications, when you make a change on your iPad, iPhone on your desktop application, the change shows up immediately on all devices without any further effort on the user’s part. 

Due does not work like this. When you check off an item that has been completed it does not show up on the other devices. For example, the alarm on my computer, iPad and iPhone go off. On my iPhone I tick off that I have done the task. But the alarm on my iPad and my computer keep going off saying the task is undone, requiring me to go into each device and check them off yet again.

Due's "sync" claim refers to a ineffective and inadequate process by which each device, when you make a change, makes a usually-unsuccessful attempt to sync only when you start the program or close it. If you wait days or weeks to open/close Due on another device, it will not have synched. Even in the rare times when it succeeds in completing a faux sync, when you open the program on another device, it still says your task is incomplete, until it gives you a message "downloading" and then it says "updated" and that task goes away.

Second, if there is an alarm that you need to keep going off until you have completed the task, you have only two options for the frequency of that alarm: “every minute” or “every hour.” So I either get bombed every single minute to complete a task or I get reminded in an hour when it’s too late to complete certain tasks. No other option, and no customizability with this “default snooze” on the iPad/iPhone apps.

But to make matters worse, the application on desktop does have this customizability (only available on the desktop/laptop), but it doesn’t transfer to the iPhone/iPad, defeating the whole purpose of having it on the mobile devices unless you are in the same room as your laptop/desktop (with them booted) all day and night.  

I feel that due to the application’s inaccurate description on the App and iTunes store, anyone who wants a refund should be granted one. I plan to ask for one today, and am crossing my fingers that Apple does the right thing by
1. Granting me a refund, and
2. Requiring the manufacturer to change its claim that it syncs to iCloud.

What I like:
* The simplicity - I do not need this to be my to-do list
* iCloud Sync
* Seeing reminders in order of soonest to latest
* Great interface

I only have one request - the app really needs to have the ability to pre-alert. I want to be able to use this to remind of doctors appointments, etc. and it's useless to be alerted at the time of the appointment. If I set up the reminder for a time or date before the appointment, I have to type the actual time/date into the reminder, which detracts from the ease of use. Reading the FAQ, I see that the developer does not want to add pre-alerts, presumably in the name of keeping things simple, but I really think this would be a great addition, and would not add to the complexity since the reminders would still default to reminding at the time and date of the reminder. It would just be an extra feature for those who would like it. Yes, I could do these appointments in a calendaring app, but to me, they fit into the reminder category, and I like to see them there.

So I would set a task, and it would keep bugging me until I completed the task, not just send me one notification, like many of the other apps for the iPhone, or the apple one.  Because those apps just didn't work for me ultimately, actually had to pull out my old wm6 phone and start using it again just for the task functionality. Sad, but true….
I don't know how long Due has been out, but I'm very thankful I found it, it finally gives enough functionality or reminders to actually keep on top of me/remind me until I complete the task.
I have to give it 5 stars for having the functionality that I truly needed.  But it would be even better if they could get iCloud working like the apple reminders work, so I don't have to open the app to sync it.

title: For some users-great, for others-not perfect
body:
If you use one device only, then Due is probably great for your needs.  I would like a note box added to an entry for info like phone numbers, address, whatever.  Having one line for the name and anything else you may need can be limiting.  If you don't have such a need, then Due is a 5-STAR app for now (read below).

If you use several devices (iPad and iPhone in my case), then Due is three stars, since you don't get push syncing of a reminder from one device to another.  You have to manual close/open the app in order to trigger a sync or do a manual sync.  Another poster mentioned that he used another alert app to remind him to trigger a sync of Due on the second device.

When I first looked into Due, I thought this tied into Reminders in iOS and iCal - not so.  It's independent of that.  With mountain lion coming and its tie into reminders on iOS, Due may well be a temp app that has value until that day.  We'll see.  At any rate, consider Due's feature carefully before buying.  If you use only one device, then it will work well for you.  Otherwise, you'll have to do some thinking about this.  I also think the price for the iOS version of Due is at the upper end for this app.  The OSX version of Due has severe limitations and is richly priced for what it offers.  Be sure to read reviews at the Mac App Store if you think you'd like both the iOS and OSX versions for a synced system.

body: This app does exactly what I need it to do.  LOCAL reminders (not server-based, push reminders), with the nagging that I need .  My only complaint is the auto snooze timing.  Either every minute or every hour is a bit extreme.  I often leave my iPad at my desk at work when I'm doing other things.  1 minute snoozes can be annoying to others who have to hear the reminder sounds.  I read the reasons why the developer won't (or can't) program for anything in between, but a 1 minute snooze is too often if I'm in the middle of something else when the reminder fires.  1 hour is too long for a snooze.  Even if the developer is not willing to code around the API limitations to allow multiple snoozes outside of 1 minute or 1 hour, something in between would be a great addition (like 10 minutes).  I don't like to penalize a developer for a system limitation, but from a usability perspective, that is the only thing that keeps this app from earning a perfect 5 stars from me.  Everything else is on point.

My recent iPad purchase coupled with a much busier routine from last year I have found recurring reminders necessary and have come to realize that Due is fantastic at those, too! Hourly, daily, weekly, yearly.... I've set up reminders when to start my exercise routine, start my housework, what chore to do first, back up my computer as well as take my blood pressure and start dinner! All of these plus the addition of my impromptu reminders that pop up daily and it never misses a beat or gets me confused. Seamlessly syncs with my iPod for when I leave the house and backs up with Dropbox...... I'm always on time and completely organized throughout my day!

title: Please ADD easy ON/OFF switch to make "relay-race"  triggered timers!
body:
This application is amazing but one thing that would make my life 100x easier is if you could add a easy ON/OFF switch to make the timers dependent on the previous timer…. sort of like a relay race!!

For example, if I have 3 timers -- A, B, and C -- timer B will not be set in motion until timer A is triggered. Say I timer A is set to "do homework for 30 mins"…. once the 30 minutes are up…. then timer B, which is "do 1 hour of cardio" will be set in motion. Logically, when I have a ton of things to do, I create a list of tasks and pick them off one after the other. This would simulate that perfectly. There may be a setting in between that gives you X amount of in-between time (let's say 5 minutes… although it could be changed) so you can switch gears but this would be PHENOMENAL!!

If added, this would be an AWESOME FEATURE!!

title: Excellent!! Can Think Of Only One Suggestion!
body:
I'm using Due in conjunction with 2Do (one of those complicated to do lists) to great effect -- the two complement each other perfectly!

I can only find one suggestion which would make a HUGE difference for me. If you're away for your device for a while and you have a number of items come due, you have to tap the screen for as many times as you've had alarms go off. And while you're trying to get through them, if you take longer than a minute to resolve all of them, those with one minute snoozes start going off all over again. So, my suggestion is: along with the "Close" and "View" buttons, it would be great to have a "snooze all 10 minutes," button or something like that, or maybe a "Close All" button, so that you don't have to cycle through all the alerts before being able to work the list.

Other than that, it's fantastic, probably my most-used app overall! Thanks for a GREAT product!

title: Recommended buy
body:
Like many others here, I'm using it daily. Until we have chip implants, I think this must be the most intuitive way to instantly turn a "gosh I have to..."-thought into a digital reminder. This app sets the benchmark for all other reminders, may it be as stand alone app or as feature inside another app (or site). 

The only thing I would change is the retro art deco striped background. (That's how hard it is to find anything critical to say about it) But actually I'm not looking at the app long enough during average usage to even notice it. (That's how fast it is.) 

Congratulation and thanks to the creators for a great app. 

*Gazing into the stars and thinking about future versions*..   like others, I use the timer function rarely. It's well done, but I keep forgetting that I have it. Strategically, functions like this might eventually find a more intuitive home either inside reminders (with a fifth "minute" dial?) or in separate little apps (or app shortcuts) sitting in separate "daily action" layers (or dimensions) of our future desktops. I'd like to see the space of the current timer button then be used for statistics, showing me what things I often need reminding for in my life and in what intervals etc. This app is so good, it would deserve this kind of back end expansion.

title: Perfect for the little things
body:
The latest update includes every feature I'd asked for in my last review, so 5 stars it is! :)

--------------------

Let me preface this by saying that Due is in no way a task manager - it's all about the little things. I use Things for my full-featured task manager.

Due is great for the stuff that falls through the cracks or clutters up a calendar/task manager - stuff like "rotate the laundry" or "mail mortgage payment," etc - things that need to get done at a specific time and are easy to check off or postpone for a few minutes right then and there. It uses local notifications and does a wonderful job of syncing between devices, and has a beautiful UI (although the tiny icons are unintuitive at first).

The one thing I would love to see is a more robust calendar scheduling system, with options like "Every First Monday" instead of just "Repeat every 15th". This would be much more helpful for some of the typical types of repeating tasks (like time sheets, dry cleaning, etc).

title: Pure elegance, flawless execution
body:
What could be a better mark of craftsmanship than shipping  an app that does something this "simple"—but which is designed and executed so thoughtfully that it can perform this supposedly simple thing in the most elegant, intelligent, and friction-free way imaginable. 

Due is there when you need it, it's blazingly fast to use, and then it gets and stays the heck out of your way. 

Like Instapaper, GoodReader, and Pastebot, Due is an essential piece of my iOS workflow that I can't imagine NOT using daily. And, I can highly recommend trying it for yourself. 

For every 500 iOS apps that the whackers slap together as a crashy and derivative $.99 "Hello World," there's maybe one or two as swell as Due. Maybe.

This is the sort of app that our friends at Apple should be putting in every demo to demonstrate the hard and careful work that the best iOS devs are shipping—apps that do all the heavy lifting to prove that iOS has the potential to become a truly first-class platform. 

If I could, I'd give Due 11 stars, a free steak dinner, and an embarrassingly sloppy French kiss. Bravo.

title: The only to do app I use
body:
I have gone through a lot of to do apps with time with an iPod touch. shortly before getting my iPhone I saw this app advertised in a Macworld newsletter. I got it and now it's the only to do app I use or even need. It's so fast and simple to make a reminder, and I have several preset timers, like moving the laundry from the washer to the dryer that I use a lot.  This app is totally worth three bucks. I certainly recommend it.

New version: I do like the double tap to edit feature and the fact that you don't have to edit a reminder to change the snooze and alarm features. I would however like to see more options for snooze other than one minute or one hour. The fact that it's only those two options makes me hardly ever use the snooze feature. 
I would also recommend being able to sync with Mail and iCal's to do list so that I can see what I have to do on my computer and set reminders on my computer to later be used in Due. Overall though great update.

title: Good but could be improved
body:
I use Due on the iPad and iPhone.  I often check off an item on one device and a bit later get a reminder to do it on the other. I wish it had an option to sync periodically when the app is up instead of just on open and close. Perhaps it should try to sync before displaying a reminder?

It would be really nice if you had the option of snoozing directly from the reminder that pops up.  Now you have to view and then snooze the particular reminder.  

It is annoying that you have to set the time of the reminder first in some cases. If the time in the reminder is earlier than right now, it automatically rolls the date to tomorrow.  A brief delay in rolling this date would be handy.

I don't like that it reorders the list after each tap of snooze.  If I have another reminder that becomes due before the result of adding snooze to the current reminder, it reorders them and I end up tapping on the wrong reminder.  I would suggest putting in a delay of 3-5 seconds before reordering the list after snooze.  If I'm going to snooze multiple times, it should fall within that window.

I use Quick Access Timings all the time.  Very handy.

There is a bit of wasted space on the iPad version.  If I have reminders up, there is about 2" of space (vertically) that is unused on the left side of the panel.  I would suggest either having it fill the panel or putting the settings panel there when it is brought up.  Right now, settings is a floating panel.

Nice that it syncs with Dropbox.

Overall good and useful. Worth the $5 in my opinion.

The icons are cute but this app was supposed to cut the BS and get to the point. Not so here. Drop cute and don't make me think about interface. Also, three, the timer should start when I tell it to. Just because I prepared a timer does not mean I want it to start as soon as I am finished making it. It would be nice to have auto-start as an option, but not as your only choice. All in all, great app. I use it all the time.
Thank you.

title: Excellent, excellent app!
body:
This app does one thing, and one thing only: It bring a reliable recurring alarm to the iPhone. This is something that caused me a great deal of hesitation before I bought the iPhone (when my Treo finally died on me).  For all the wonderful features of the iPhone, having no recurring alarm that can be easily and quickly set makes it practically useless for me in many ways. So I had been searching every other day on the app store for an app like this one. Sure, it would have been nice if this simple function was an integral part of the iPhone OS (calendar or its native alarm), but since neither the iPhone calendar nor the native alarm has this function--an indispensable function for me, I am more than thrilled to have found this app. 

The recurring alarm keeps going off after a set interval--until you turn it off or reset the time. It has several quick-access buttons that allow you to delay the alarm for 10 minutes, an hour, or a day. Once the alarm is canceled, there is a "Logbook" where all the previous alarms are kept--which can be deleted if you so choose, but otherwise, the canceled ("Done") alarms are not visible.

title: Great app - excellent support
body:

Only thing that would make this better is smaller increments of snooze times. 10 or 15 minutes would be perfect. The developer (who replied to my feedback extremely quickly and professionally) told me that this was due to limitations on apple's end though so doesn't look like there is much to do about it.

author: ScottMcGerik

title: Great App - More Sounds Please
body:
Update: I'm updating my review because as time goes on, I use this app more and more. It's so useful for a variety of reminders and timers. Really helps me stay organized and on top of the things. The only thing I ask for is more sounds!

The update definitely improves the functionality of this app by allowing shorter than 15 minute intervals. While I do find myself using this app on a daily basis, keep in mind that it's only good for setting quick reminders/alerts. If you want more structured or detailed reminders with a snooze option, stick to the calendar alerts in the native calendar app.

body:
I absolutely love this app!!!  Its easy to set up and no clutter.

But, I don't like the sounds I have to choose from; the long sounds are not very imaginative and the short sounds are much to short.  I don't want to hear another old fashioned phone ring, nor do I want a hurricane warning as the only sounds that last longer than 4 seconds.  
Please add more choices and the ability to change the length of each and every sound.

author: Bill favor

title: Already can't do without it.
body: There are certain situations where I want to be reminded of something, but don't want to clutter nor take the time to put it in my calendar. A phone call I need to make later today, a tv show I want to see tomorrow night, etc. It doesn't take the place of a full fledged task manager or a calendar. It's great at doing exactly what the app claims to do. It's a nice supplement to my workflow and fits a niche need quite well. Well worth the money for me.

author: rebrim

title: Excellent and quick
body:
Just yesterday I needed a quick reminder for an event a couple of hours away and I went into Calendar and it required a ton of steps to do it. With Due, it would have taken seconds.

I love the interface and that there's a difference between timers and reminders, especially the way it saves and lets you reuse them.

Perhaps it's a bit pricey for such a single-function app (though I feel silly complaining about something less than the price of a cup of coffee), and I would like it to add recurring reminders (e.g. weekly, bimonthly, etc), but definitely a useful, well-done app.
